text: This section provides an overview of 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS) product family, describing the configurations, system profile and network solutions of the system. This document focuses on the support of 1830 PSS-8, 1830 PSS-16, 1830 PSS-16II, 1830 PSS-32, 1830 PSI-4L and 1830 PSI-8L. The shelves 1830 PSS-36, 1830 PSS-64 and 1830 PSS-8x/12x/24x are contained in this document in some general descriptions, for example in configurations, as they are used to build cluster configurations. Refer to 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-4) Release 23.6 Product Information and Planning Guide, 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-36/PSS-64) Release 14.1 Product Information and Planning Guide and 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-8x/ PSS-12x/PSS-24x) Release 23.6 Product Information and Planning Guide for detailed feature support on the other shelf types of the product family. The system supports two software load-lines: SWDM software and OCS software. Each software load-line may support only a subset of the shelves. In order to indicate under which software load-line a shelf is operated, the shelf name is followed by the load-line name in brackets: PSS-xy (SWDM) or PSS-xy (OCS).

section_path: 1 System concept > 1.2 System configuration > 1.2.2 SWDM NE
text: The 1830 PSS shelves provide increased network flexibility and operational automation through zero-touch, transparent photonic networking. Photonic networks use simplified and accelerated operations to transform wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) into true transport networking with advanced flexibility, performance, automation, and integration. Several Optical Add-Drop multiplexing (OADM) configurations are supported by components that provide optical filter routing, optical amplification, and support for interworking with optical signals originating on non-1830 PSS hardware. The PSS-8/PSS-16/PSS-16II/PSS-32/PSI-8L are closely related shelves that compose the PSS-32/ PSS-16 multi-service multi-reach solution. They are scalable optical transport platforms that implement a converged platform solution for multi-service DWDM metro-area, long-haul, and Optical Transport Network (OTN) switching, and leading edge flexibility with next generation optical and OTN capabilities. • The 1830 PSS-8 end office shelf provides an 8-slot SWDM platform in 3-RU footprint, with additional distributed switching functionality. • The 1830 PSS-16 end office shelf provides a 16-slot SWDM platform in 8-RU footprint. • The 1830 PSS-16II end office shelf provides the second generation 16-slot SWDM platform in 8-RU footprint (DC variant) or 9-RU footprint (AC/DC variant), with additional distributed switching functionality. • The 1830 PSS-32 central office shelf provides a 32-slot high-capacity and high-scalability core SWDM platform in 14-RU footprint. • The 1830 PSS-8x central office shelf provides an 8-slot high-capacity and high-scalability DWDM platform with optical core switching functionality.

section_path: 1 System concept > 1.2 System configuration > 1.2.6 Node Scalability
text: Node scalability refers to the ability of the 1830 PSS system to combine three or more NEs into one cluster under one common main SWDM NE. For example: • OCS NE + OCS NE + SWDM NE • SWDM NE + SWDM NE The main shelf of the main NE controls all transponders and uplink cards of the cluster. On each cluster NE, unique user-assigned NE names for the other cluster NEs that will be connected must be defined and associated with their IP Addresses. NEs with optical line resources can perform auto power management for OT line ports on other NEs. General management functions continue to be performed by the individual NEs which contain the OTs.

In order to manage data synchronization between cluster NEs, this feature supports an audit function that is performed by the main NE against each tributary NE where it has connections. For parameters set by the main NE on the tributary NE: • If the audit finds a disagreement, the main NE must re-provision the tributary NE to the values determined to be correct by the main NE. For parameters where the main NE only reads from the tributary NE (but never sets): • If the audit finds a disagreement, the main NE must re-provision its own values to agree with the tributary NE. The main NE is responsible for setting port-level wavetracker values, power values, and channel values as necessary for managing transmission on tributary NEs. The main NE performs an audit/sync against tributary NE data: • Every time the communication link comes up, including main NE boot-up. • Periodically, a frequency that does not harm system performance, enables an audit 15 minutes after the current audit has finished (in normal circumstances, depending on system load). The cluster audit checks data out-of-sync conditions on existing ports, and fixes the problems whenever possible. All out-of-sync conditions are flagged by raising local audit alarms, regardless of whether fixed or not.

section_path: 1 System concept > 1.3 System profile > 1.3.3 UCM support for 3 OCS nodes
text: UCM (Uplink Card Management) is the WDM software module responsible for the following functions: • Managing the WDM-OCS communications interface • Provisioning and monitoring OCS uplink services • Integrating OCS uplink data into the WDM system • Translating between WDM and OCS views of the uplink data UCM allows the WDM system to directly control the optical characteristics (for example, frequency, wavekeys, dynamic power levels) of the OCS uplink ports as needed to integrate the uplink channels into the WDM lines. Connections between OCS uplink ports and DWDM optical ports are defined by “inter-NE” optical connections. UCM supports uplink connections to SFD channel ports, CWR CLS ports, OPSA SIG ports, MCS AD ports, and PSC add/drop ports. UCM provides and maintains an internal uplink proxy model which allows all other WDM software (including GMPLS CP) to interface to OCS uplink cards. UCM is supported on 1830 PSS32/PSS16 shelf types, and maintains an NE- to-NE interface with up to three OCS NEs. WDM-OCS transmission fibers can connect to any 1830 PSS shelf which contains WDM optics (except PSS-4).

Wavelength Tracker optical performance monitoring Wavelength Tracker enables next-generation optical networks through protected wavelengths and extension to higher-degree nodes. section_path: 1 System concept > 1.3 System profile > 1.3.7 Low-cost traffic transport
text: Flexible IP traffic grooming options at the OTN layer, including port-level and sub-port-level grooming, enable efficient core-router traffic offload onto the optical network and support scaling of the IP backbone. Designed to ensure efficient bandwidth management and traffic forwarding at the most economical transport layer, the 1830 PSS meets the challenge of explosive service growth by facilitating traffic transport at the lowest cost per bit - while ensuring the highest availability and resiliency for service quality assurance. The advanced GMPLS-based automation capabilities expand operational efficiencies across the optical and IP layers and help minimize service providers' total cost of ownership (TCO).

section_path: 1 System concept > 1.3 System profile > 1.3.9 Green networking
text: The 1830 PSS enables automated operations and resilience with an integrated Generalized Multi- Protocol Label Switching (GMPLS) control plane. The 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS) also increases network monetization by reducing the resources required for protection and freeing bandwidth for revenue-producing traffic. With the use of technology innovations, 1830 PSS brings a number of eco-benefits in addition to CAPEX and OPEX advantages. Specifically, it provides for: • Lower network power consumption as the platform manages traffic at the most economical transport layer by combining silicon innovation, OTN bandwidth management capabilities and GMPLS-enabled cross layer intelligence for resource optimization • Delegation of several management processes to the control plane for automation including discovery processes for network topology, resources and services, end-to-end connection routing, flow-through service provisioning, and mesh restoration • Intelligent restoration mechanisms boosting network reliability, allowing network failures and fiber cuts to be accumulated and fixed in batches instead of one at a time. This allowance for planned network maintenance activities reduces the cost of on-site maintenance as well as travel-related CO2 emissions • Fewer site visits for provisioning • A smaller footprint • “Green” FPGA images – for port groups which are not used, an image is loaded that causes nearly no power consumption • Pluggable optical modules that only need to be installed if in use or planned

text: 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS) helps network providers to introduce the scalable, unified photonic and electronic transport networking as defined in the Optical Transport Network (OTN) hierarchy. Figure 1-5 OTN basic principles ODU switching ODU switching Electronic domain 1...N 1...N WDM switching WDM switching Photonic domain Line Line 1...N Amplifier Amplifier 1...N Optical Transport Section (OTS) Optical Multiplex Section (OMS) - multi-wavelengths Optical Channel (Och) - wavelength Optical Data Unit (ODU) - sub-wavelength The Optical Channel (OCh) provides end-to-end bandwidth management for a wavelength signal in the photonic domain. The Optical Data Unit (ODU) provides end-to-end bandwidth management for a sub-wavelength signal in the electronic domain. The ODU is a fixed-sized container with in-band OAM tools for quality supervision and SLA assurance. The ODU functions as primary bearer for client traffic. Higher-order ODU (HO-ODU) transparently carries multiple (multiplexed) lower-order ODUs which can transport 1.25 Gb/s, 2.5 Gb/s, or 10 Gb/s client signal rates.

section_title: Regional interconnects of an OTN backbone
section_path: 1 System concept > 1.5 Network solutions > 1.5.2 Regional interconnects of an OTN backbone
text: In this example, the OTN backbone of a complex network is built with 1830 PSS network elements which act as a gateway to SDH/SONET regions or to other OTN networks. Advantages of this architecture include the following: • The OTN backbone is flexible in interconnecting existing regional networks. • The OTN backbone is independent of service types. • Different services are aggregated into OTN granularity. • The SDH/SONET ↔ OTN gateway is realized in a single node, either SDH ↔ OTN or SONET ↔ OTN. In the current software release, the SDH or the SONET mode can be configured on card level. The SDH/SONET gateway function also supports terminated SDH/SONET (that is, switching on STSn, VCn level). • 1+1 ODUk path protection (SNC/N) on the network ports is available in the current software release, the system is prepared to support additional protection mechanisms in future releases. • 1+1 ODUk non-intrusive client protection (ODUk SNC/Nc) is compatible for interworking with SDH/SONET MSP/APS protection. section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.1 WDM shelf overview > 2.1.1 Overview
text: The 1830 PSS shelves provide the framework where WDM application NEs are constructed. The 1830 PSS shelves can be deployed as a single-shelf NE, a main shelf, or an extension shelf as the need arises. The 1830 PSS shelves each provide card slots, fiber management trays, backplane, power distribution, and cooling. The first shelf of an NE, designated by a reserved Shelf ID value, becomes the main shelf and provides the management and control connections to the operations systems for the cluster of shelves in a multi-shelf NE. Expansion shelves connect to the main shelf through protected internal LAN communication links and provide extended slot capacity managed by the single database that resides in the main shelf. Refer Table 5-1, “List of 1830 PSS items ” (p. 1080) for details on the supported cards in different shelf types.

text: Each 1830 PSS shelf contains several universal slots for application cards, two slots designated for controller cards that are configured for redundant control, two slots designated for power filter cards and fan units for cooling. The shelves also have customer interface panels, most of which contain a rotary switch to configure the Shelf ID for multiple shelf installations. Refer to 2.1.4 “Shelf identification” (p. 75). Each application card slot supports two card interfaces per slot, allowing them to accept two half height cards in each slot when that slot is also equipped with a half-slot adapter (HSLAD). For a description of the other supported SWDM shelves refer to the 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-4) Release 23.6 Product Information and Planning Guide and to the 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-8x/PSS-12x/PSS-24x) Release 23.6 Product Information and Planning Guide. Mandatory shelf equipment Each shelf contains mandatory modules with which it must be equipped. Mandatory equipment will be automatically provisioned whether present or not. Each 1830 PSS-8, 1830 PSS-16, 1830 PSS- 16II and 1830 PSS-32 shelf includes the following mandatory equipment: • One shelf controller (EC) (can be in either EC slot) • Two power modules (PF) • A fan module (FAN) • User interface panel (USRPNL) is mandatory on the main shelf only, and not supported on other shelves

Each application card slot supports two card interfaces per slot, allowing them to accept two half height cards in each slot when that slot is also equipped with a half-slot adapter (HSLAD). For a description of the other supported SWDM shelves refer to the 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-4) Release 23.6 Product Information and Planning Guide and to the 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-8x/PSS-12x/PSS-24x) Release 23.6 Product Information and Planning Guide. Mandatory shelf equipment Each shelf contains mandatory modules with which it must be equipped. Mandatory equipment will be automatically provisioned whether present or not. Each 1830 PSS-8, 1830 PSS-16, 1830 PSS- 16II and 1830 PSS-32 shelf includes the following mandatory equipment: • One shelf controller (EC) (can be in either EC slot) • Two power modules (PF) • A fan module (FAN) • User interface panel (USRPNL) is mandatory on the main shelf only, and not supported on other shelves

text: Some 1830 PSS network elements that do not reside physically within a slot of a universal shelf are modeled as separate shelves and depend upon inventory cable connections for integrated monitoring. The maximum number of passive shelves that can be daisy-chained to an LD/WR card is 10 with the furthest inventory port at 40m distance. In this case, the network element can not detect its removal from the system.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.1 WDM shelf overview > 2.1.4 Shelf identification
text: All shelves in a network element must have a unique Shelf ID set by the hardware Shelf ID switch. The Shelf ID determines the identity and role of each universal shelf in a cluster. To configure the Shelf ID, the 1830 PSS-8, 1830 PSS-16, 1830 PSS-16II and 1830 PSS-32 shelves have physical mechanisms, called rotary dials, located on the backplane. Each shelf has 2 rotary dials. The 1830 PSI-4L and 1830 PSI-8L shelves are not provided with rotary dials to pre-configure the Shelf ID individually per shelf, on site prior to powering up the shelf. Instead, they use a software based function to specify and maintain the Shelf ID in a multi-shelf NE. The Shelf ID value is written by factory with a default into a PSI-L SEEPROM.

Single-shelf layout A single-shelf network element (NE) consists of one 1830 PSS-8, 1830 PSS-16 , 1830 PSS-16II or 1830 PSS-32 shelf acting as a main shelf. Main/multiple shelf operation When used in a multiple-shelf configuration, each 1830 PSS shelf has a Shelf ID number that is configured through the physical mechanism (two rotary dials on each shelf). The most significant bit of the rotary dial determines its role (main or extension shelf). The rotary dial for each shelf must be set to a valid value; this value must be unique within the same NE. The values of the rotary dial are interpreted as follows. Bits 4-3-2-1-0 code the Shelf ID Number. An integer in the range 0-31 is possible, but the current maximum number of shelves supported for an NE is 24. section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.1 WDM shelf overview > 2.1.5 Management connections between main and extension shelves
text: The equipment controllers on 1830 PSS shelves provide all node and shelf control and management functions for a shelf. The functions performed by the controller depend on the shelf where it resides. The first active shelf is the “main” shelf. The controller in the main shelf is the main controller, and it provides the LAN interfaces to external management systems and extension shelves. The controller maintains the persistent database and configures all shelves and packs in the NE accordingly, and it also monitors their health. A controller in a extension shelf is called a extension controller, which coordinates all communication within its shelf and communicates fault and performance data back to the main controller. Flash cards (required) in extension controllers are automatically upgraded along with the main controller when software upgrades are performed. Management connectivity between shelves is done through Ethernet ports on the controllers. Main and extension configurations are supported as shown in following table. text: The 1830 Photonic Service Switch shelves may be equipped with redundant equipment controllers (EC). Extension shelves that are connected to a main shelf operating redundant ECs also must be equipped with redundant ECs. Refer to Table 2-1, “ Main and non-universal extension shelf combinations” (p. 76) for the supported shelf combinations. The following information describes wired equipment that is available to support the 1830 PSS-16 and 1830 PSS-32 shelves. Fiber storage tray (FST) The Fiber Storage Tray is rack-mountable and is used for managing excess cable lengths within the boundaries of the rack. DCM shelf (DCMSHFxx) The DCM shelf is a rack-mountable tray used for holding multiple DCM modules. There is one version that is mountable in 19-inch racks (DCMSHF19) and one in ETSI and ANSI (23-inch) racks (DCMSHF23). The number of DCMs that a shelf can house depends on the rack type and DCM type (length). Attenuator drawer (ATTNDRW) The attenuator drawer is a 1 RU-high rack-mountable tray for storage of up to 24 attenuators of any size, if/when attenuators are needed for FOADM nodes.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.2 1830 PSS-8 shelf > 2.2.5 Backplane
text: Refer to Table 5-2, “Slot ranges per card/shelf type ” (p. 1109) for the cards that are supported in the 1830 PSS-8 shelf. The 1830 PSS-8 backplane delivers 100Gb/s of transmission bandwidth from each I/O slot to the correlative slots in the shelf. Controllers on the EC cards are connected to the I/O slots by 100Mb/s Ethernet links configured in a redundant star network. Various serial buses complete the control plane to handle the infrastructure functions. The 1830 PSS-8 backplane is compatible with the 1830 PSS-32/16 shelves, therefore all cards designed for 1830 PSS-32/16 shelves can be supported on 1830 PSS-8/16II shelves. section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.3 1830 PSS-16 shelf > 2.3.1 Introduction
text: The 1830 PSS-16 shelf provides a 16-slot SWDM platform in 8-RU footprint. The shelf supports redundant control, redundant power and interfaces for management, maintenance, synchronization, and alarms. The 16 universal slots are arranged in two rows of 8, on either side of each other. There are 21 total slots, including slots for Equipment Controllers, Power Filters, and fans. For detailed specifications, such as physical design, weight and power consumption, refer to Chapter 7, “Technical specifications” Figure 2-8 1830 PSS-16 shelf

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.4 1830 PSS-16II shelf > 2.4.5 Backplane
text: Refer to Table 5-2, “Slot ranges per card/shelf type ” (p. 1109) for the cards that are supported in the 1830 PSS-16II shelf. The 1830 PSS-16II backplane consists of two QUADs; four slots in one QUAD are fully interconnected by 2x100G. The backplane delivers 100Gb/s of transmission bandwidth from each half I/O slot to the correlative slots within each quad. Figure 2-12 1830 PSS-16II backplane high speed connectivity Legend: Red arrow N-N+3 connection Blue arrow N-N+1 connection Yellow arrow N-N+2 connection Light blue arrow 11OPE8 & 11QCE12X Mate Port backplane connectivity The controllers on the EC cards are connected to the I/O slots by 100Mb/s Ethernet links configured in a redundant star network. The 1830 PSS-16II backplane is compatible with the current PSS-32/16, therefore all cards designed for the PSS-32/16 shelves can be supported on the 1830 PSS-16II shelf. For the 1830 PSS-16II shelf, within each quad, there are extra different reserved connections between any two vertical half-height service slots besides the high speed traffic connections - 2 bi-directional differential lanes (or 4 uni-directional differential pairs) for high speed OHI (HS_OHI) with a speed up to 6.25 Gbps. Service power V3.6 is provided to all slots on the shelf. Each PF contains a 3.3V DC/DC converter that provides the V3.6 service voltage that is distributed by the backplane.

section_title: 1830 PSS-16II shelf with support for integrated AC or DC power supply
section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.4 1830 PSS-16II shelf > 2.4.7 1830 PSS-16II shelf with support for integrated AC or DC power supply
text: The following graphic shows the details related to the configuration of the AC/DC rectifiers for 1830 PSS-16II: Figure 2-13 AC/DC rectifier configuration details options The 1830 PSS-16II supports an integrated AC/DC power filter module. The AC power filters operate in a 1+1 protected configuration and the AC power should be greater than 2000W. Simplified timing is required. The 1830 PSS-16II AC shelf variant supports unrestricted configuration with AC power (up to 2.5kW). The maximum system power consumption is planned around 2460W to support the 8 OT slots with power consumption of maximum 240W per slot. The PF-AC card consists of 2 independent boards: the power board for AC/DC and DC/DC conversion and LED control, the timing/control board for S-CRU and other control circuit. There is no direct electrical connection between them, but go through backplane. Physically they are bound together and logically NE SW shall treat it as an integrated card. The user panel and the FAN for the 1830 PSS-16II AC shelf is similar to that of the PSS-16II shelf. The 2 power and timing slots of 1830 PSS-16II AC shelf is extended than that of AB shelf. The height is increased and more connectors are added. Shelf overview The 1830 PSS-16II AC shelf is a 9RU high shelf and can fit into 300 mm depth rack.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.6 1830 PSI-4L shelf > 2.6.1 Introduction
text: The 1830 PSI-4L shelf is a high-capacity compact, modular shelf type under the PSI branch of the 1830 product family, intended for WDM line system applications. The 1830 PSI-4L can support up to four full-height or up to eight half-height universal I/O cards when that slot is also equipped with a half-slot adapter. It additionally supports two redundant AC power modules, or two redundant DC power filters, a Multi-Function Card (MFC) which houses the equipment controllers and a rear-facing user panel. The front of the shelf also contains a front-facing user panel. For detailed specifications, such as physical design, weight and power consumption, refer to Chapter 7, “Technical specifications”. Figure 2-17 1830 PSI-4L shelf Note: All slots must be equipped with either a function card or a passive blank face-plate to ensure proper airflow for the cooling system.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.8 Control architecture > 2.8.2 System control
text: The active Equipment Controller (EC) on shelves provides all node and shelf control and management functions and handles the interfaces to management systems. The second EC card is standby and capable to take over the role of an active EC once the formerly active EC becomes inactive. Each EC contains a Micro-controller asset (MCA) and other devices to support the required functionality. The MCA of the EC consists of a processor (CPU) with interface logic and is integrated into the EC motherboard. All system components contain a client control function (CCF) that allow them to operate independently once configured and placed into operation. This function is used for application configuration / reporting (where applicable), inventory control, FPGA download (where applicable), and card status retrieval. Figure 2-23 Control schematic CCF Client control function CRU Clock recovery unit LSW LAN switch board MCA Micro-controller asset

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.8 Control architecture > 2.8.3 Multi-shelf configurations
text: From a control architecture perspective, the SWDM NE and the OCS NE are separate sets of shelves, only interconnected through external interfaces. Also the inter-NE TL1 communication for uplink card management runs through external interfaces (usually through OAMP LAN). Both NEs must be connected through an external router that allows this communication or through external LAN switch. Refer to the 1830 PSS Installation and System Turn-Up Guide (ITG). Inside each NE, shelves are interconnected through dual LAN rings. Refer to the “Shelf interconnection” section in the 1830 PSS-36/64 Product Information and Planning Guide.

A single ECC is associated with a single Network Interface (NETIF). Up to 128 NETIFs are supported per NE, and among them only 64 NETIFs can be associated with any given shelf. section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.10 External communications: LAN > 2.10.1 User service interfaces
text: The 1830 PSS provides LAN interfaces for management access and debug, and for the access to the management communication network (MCN). Management access is provided for 1830 PSS ZIC for a system with OCS or both OCS and SWDM NEs, and for WebUI for a system that is only SWDM NE. LAN interface for 1830 PSS ZIC/WebUI access The “CIT” connector is on the front panel of each Equipment Controller (EC) and is available for WebUI or Local Craft access. CIT access is only possible in the main shelf. OAMP interface A single RJ-45 OAMP interface is located on the User panel. AUX interface An AUX interface is located on the Equipment Controller. This RJ-45 connector can be used for a WebUI or local Craft terminal connection. ES1/ES2 interface The ES1 and ES2 interfaces are located on the Equipment Controller. Note: In the 1830 PSI-4L/PSI-8L shelves, the ES1 and ES2 interfaces are located on the Multi-function card (PSILMFC).

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.10 External communications: LAN > 2.10.4 Addressing in SWDM NEs (1830 PSS)
text: 1830 PSS supports one provisionable LAN IP address for the active EC. Network connections on 1830 PSS-32/PSS-16 SWDM NE are supported by ports on the USRPNL and Equipment Controller (EC). For detailed information about User Panel equipment, refer to “User panels” (p. 197). USRPNL The 1830 PSS-32/PSS-16 USRPNL supports four MAC addresses stored on its EEPROM. The MAC addresses are installed and assigned at the factory and are associated with the LAN ports on the USRPNL. Replacement of the USRPNL will cause new MAC addresses to be associated with these LAN ports. External IP address and MAC address are fixed and follow the active LAN ports on the USRPNL. There are four ports on the user panel: OAMP, VOIP, E1 and E2. Each of these four ports have four MAC addresses. • OAMP: connection to management systems through an external DCN • VOIP: connection of an IP-phone • E1/E2: management of external equipment The interfaces can be configured with an IPv4 and/or IPv6 address. The interfaces support a DHCP client role. When configured in this mode the interface will receive its IP address from the network.

text: note that the CIT port does not run the full set of IP features supported on the OAMP port. The CIT port only provides basic NE management for local management through SNMP. Remote NE management through the CIT port can be supported only if the operator assigns unique IP addresses to these CIT ports. Below the CIT port on the EC faceplate, the second port is labeled AUX which has the same functionality as E1, E2 and VOIP. Each AUX port carries an independent IP subnet. The bottom two ports on the EC faceplate, labeled ES1 and ES2 (ES for extension shelf), are internal ports only and are used to connect to 1830 PSS-32/PSS-16 main/primary shelves with extension shelves. The 1830 PSS NE can be comprised of multiple 1830 shelves. In order to create one NE with a single TID, these shelves are tied together in a daisy chain fashion, using the ES1 and ES2 ports. The MAC addresses of the ES1 and ES2 ports are not retrievable. Both ES ports are enabled by default, but they can be provisioned as disabled. If they are enabled with nothing is plugged in, the NE will raise an NSA condition, “Link Down,” for the ES ports.

note that the CIT port does not run the full set of IP features supported on the OAMP port. The CIT port only provides basic NE management for local management through SNMP. If they are enabled with nothing is plugged in, the NE will raise an NSA condition, “Link Down,” for the ES ports.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.11 Operation, administration, and maintenance > 2.11.7 Gateway Network Element (GNE)
text: A CLI supports all 1830 PSS system functionality. A CLI supporting GMPLS is also available, but should be used as a debug interface, or for local access. By default, GMPLS networks are managed by a network management system (NMS). The network management system can manage an 1830 PSS network while only connecting to a single NE. That NE is called a GNE and provides the management connectivity to all other remote 1830 PSS NEs (RNE) in the network via OSPF routing. 1830 PSS also supports External Border Gateway Protocol (eBGP) on the GNEs to communicate in-band routing to the DCN router in the Out-of-band (OOB) DCN. Important! It is possible to connect to the OOB DCN with either BGP or OSPF, but it is not possible to connect to the OOB DCN with both BGP or OSPF at the same time.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.11 Operation, administration, and maintenance > 2.11.9 General Communications Channel (GCC) inter-node communication
text: The OSC is a separate optical channel, operating at the STM-1/OC-3 rate of 155 Mb/s, that transfers management and control information between the ECs of two adjacent nodes, regardless of whether any of the DWDM payload channels are terminated between those two nodes. The channel is capable of transporting both IP and OSI PDUs. In CWDM and Black/White transmission link, the GCC communication channel is used for inter-node communication. 1830 PSS WDM supports GCC communication over 2.5G/10G/100G OTN links. Refer to 2.9 “External communications: ECC” (p. 113) for a detailed description.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.11 Operation, administration, and maintenance > 2.11.10 Ethernet In-Band Management Interface (ETHIF)
text: The ETHIF, available on L2 SROS packet cards, enables 1830 PSS to manage remote equipment via an Ethernet In-Band Management (IBM) VLAN. The 1830 PSS packet card acts as a gateway between the optical DCN (OAMP, OSC, or GCC interfaces) and other remote equipment that is managed via Ethernet in-band management. The IBM VLAN behaves as another Embedded Communications Channel (ECC), similar to OTN GCC or OSC; the IBM is used when a GCC or OSC is not available. Ethernet In-Band Management (IBM) is used in MPLS-TP mode on following cards: • 11QCE12X • 11OPE8 These packet cards can be configured either unprotected or protected by LAG for all cards and ERP for 11QCE12X/11OPE8.

Optical PM The system supports the monitoring and reporting of received and transmitted optical power on client and DWDM line-side interfaces. section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.11 Operation, administration, and maintenance > 2.11.13 Fault management
text: The 1830 PSS is provisionable on a per-port basis to detect/process, and report faults, failures, and performance. It is able to diagnose equipment faults down to a field replaceable unit (FRU) or interface. Transport fault processing is performed as defined in G.783 and EN 300 417. The system allows provisioning for the SONET-specific LOS/LOF handling to satisfy Telcordia GR-253 issue 3 (2000) and ANSI T1.231. There is one system default alarm profile that contains all alarms/conditions supported in the system and their severity: Critical, Major, Minor. The user can change the severity of alarms on each port/facility independently or point to the system profile. The system profile can be modified or reset to factory defaults Optical line Optical line fault processing is supported. OTN The 1830 PSS complies to G.709 for defect/fault processing of OTUk/ODUk overhead at all OTUk/ ODUk interfaces.

OTN The 1830 PSS complies to G.709 for defect/fault processing of OTUk/ODUk overhead at all OTUk/ ODUk interfaces. The following is a short summary of the main functions of the OTN. • Loss of frame (LOF) detected, causes signal fail (SF) condition and Alarm Insertion Signal (AIS) insertion. • Source and Destination Access Point Identifiers (SAPI and DAPI) are monitored. When trail Trace Identifier Mismatch (TIM) is detected, it causes a signal fail (SF) condition and AIS insertion. • Bit-interleaved parity (BIP-8) is inserted at the source. When parity violations are detected, indicating that the signal has degraded, a backward error indication (BEI) is inserted on the return to the source. • The OTN checks for error conditions and inserts the following when appropriate: AIS, Incoming Alignment Error (IAE), Backward Incoming Alignment Error Indication (BIAE), and Backward Defect Information (BDI). section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.12 IEEE 801.2AB Link Layer Discovery Protocol > 2.12.1 Overview
text: LLDP is a protocol and a set of managed objects that can be used for discovering the physical topology from adjacent stations in IEEE 802® LANs. It discovers the link-layer connectivity among Ethernet ports in a network and applies both to physical 802.3 Ethernet (ETY) ports and to virtual Ethernet ports. LLDP helps to detect and resolve network problems and inconsistencies in the configuration. On each port, LLDP can be configured for transmit and/or receive, independently for each of 3 different scopes (nearest bridge, nearest non-TPMR bridge, and nearest customer bridge) using different MAC addresses as defined in the standard. The 1830 PSS stores the information it receives from its LLDP neighbors, in the LLDP MIB. Figure 2-25 LLDP - Cross-domain management The Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) is supported on UNIs and NNIs in both access-uplink and mpls-tp modes on the 11QPE24, 11OPE8, 11QCE12X, Falcon and Sidewinder cards. Starting from PSE2s, and for all new-generation optical transponders, LLDP can only be configured for receive mode, and only for one of the three destination address groups (nearest bridge, nearest non-TPMR bridge, and nearest customer bridge). LLDP snooping supports multiple (maximum of 10) remote Media Service Access Points (MSAPs) per destination MAC address.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.14 Fan control > 2.14.1 Control mechanism
text: 1830 PSS-8/16/16II/32 fans are controlled by the active equipment controller (EC) through backplane links. The EC provisions the speed of the fan motors on the fan unit. A local microcontroller configures and monitors its associated fan motor Besides controlling the fan motor speed, the microcontrollers also collect locally generated alarms. Additionally, all of the microcontrollers have integrated temperature sensors which provide additional thermal inputs to the ECs. At normal room temperature the fans run at a reduced speed. With increasing air temperature, the fan speed increases linearly to the maximum (100 %) speed. With decreasing air temperature, the fan speed decreases accordingly. If any one of the fan motors fails, the remaining fan motors operate at full speed. If local micro controllers on fan unit fail then the associated motor goes to full speed automatically. Note: For information on the control mechanism for the PSILFAN unit used in the 1830 PSI- 4L/PSI-8L shelves, refer to 2.19 “1830 PSI-L shelf FAN unit (PSILFAN)” (p. 154).

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.15 PSS-8 Fan Unit (8FAN) > 2.15.7 FAN control and protection
text: For information on the LED on the front panel of the FAN unit, see 2.34 “LEDs of the Fan Unit” (p. 249). The Fan Unit (8FAN) is mounted at the slot 14 of the 1830 PSS-8 shelf. Noise level generated by PSS-8 shelf varies based on the card types equipped in the shelf. SW algorithm automatically adjusts the FAN speed to achieve the required air flow needed to properly cool the specific set of modules inserted in the shelf while keeping the noise generated by FAN module to a minimum level. As a result, cards that dissipate less power (<150W per slot) will require lower FAN speed and subsequently generate lower noise level than cards which exceed 150W of power dissipation. PSS-8 noise level complies with ETSI or GR-63 standards for configurations which include low power consumption cards (<150W power consumption per slot). For configurations with high power consumption card (power>150W), noise level will exceed the noise standard threshold. For further information of high level power consumption configurations and noise levels, contact Nokia. In actual deployment, FAN rotation speed will be adjusted according to the ambient temperature and power consumption of the system. SW algorithm continuously adjusts the FAN operation to minimize the noise level while achieving sufficient air flow and properly take away the heat dissipated by the inserted

User configurable parameter for 1830 PSS-8 shelf in 19 inch rack installation The 1830 PSS-8 shelf supports a configurable attribute that indicates in which rack type each shelf is installed. section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.18 PSS-32 Fan Units (FAN and FAN32H) > 2.18.2 Fan unit replacement
text: In the 1830 PSS-32 the fan unit is located directly above the function card slots. The 1830 PSS-32 fan unit contains three powerful FAN modules, each individually monitored and speed-controlled by network element (NE) software. When replacing the fan unit in an 1830 PSS-32 shelf, the only fan unit that supplies cooling air for the shelf is removed. The fan unit replacement is a simple procedure that can be accomplished in as little as 10 seconds. If the 1830 PSS-32 shelf is equipped with cards that dissipate: • ≤100W per slot, the fan unit replacement should be completed within 2 minutes. • >100W per slot and the ambient temperature is ≤25°C (77°F), the fan unit replacement should be completed within 60 seconds. • >100W per slot and the ambient temperature is >25°C (77°F), the fan unit replacement should be completed within 30 seconds. Note: Preparation time and reinstallation time (for loosening/tightening mounting screws) are not included in the time intervals stated. Refer to the Max column in Table 7-65, “Weight and power consumption for 1830 PSS” (p. 1492) for the power consumption specifications per card. Note: Some cards occupy more than one slot. Refer to the 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS) Release 23.6 Maintenance and Trouble-Clearing Guide for detailed instructions.

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.19 1830 PSI-L shelf FAN unit (PSILFAN) > 2.19.2 Control
text: The fan motors are controlled to run at the minimum speed necessary to cool the components installed. If any one of the fan motors fails, the remaining fan motors operate at full speed. Fan alarms The fan speed is supervised constantly. Any malfunctioning (including degrading of fan function) of an individual fan element is reported to the user. This includes malfunctioning where no degradation of transmission functionality is expected and malfunctioning where the transmission operation is expected to be degraded or interrupted. The alarm contains information about the degradation of fan functionality, if the system can still operate normal or not and the failure localization. The SW algorithm continuously adjusts the fan operation to minimize the noise level and the power consumption while achieving sufficient air flow and properly take away the heat dissipated by the inserted modules.

section_title: 1830 PSI-4L/PSI-8L shelf FAN noise, control and protection
section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.19 1830 PSI-L shelf FAN unit (PSILFAN) > 2.19.6 1830 PSI-4L/PSI-8L shelf FAN noise, control and protection
text: 1830 PSI-4L and 1830 PSI-8L shelves noise level complies with ETSI and GR-63 standards during normal operation of all supported configurations. The noise level generated by the 1830 PSI-4L and 1830 PSI-8L shelves varies based on the card types equipped in the shelf. Fan rotation speeds are adjusted according to the ambient temperature and power consumption of the system. A software algorithm continuously adjusts fan speeds to minimize the noise level while providing air flow sufficient to properly exhaust the system’s heat dissipation. The 1830 PSI-4L shelf supports two mandatory PSILFAN units and the 1830 PSI-8L shelf supports three mandatory PSILFAN units. Each shelf utilizes a N+1 protection scheme. Each fan unit is powered separately. When there is a single fan motor failure, the system will continue operating without a heat dissipation issue. However, all operating fan motors will run at the highest rotation speed. In this case acoustic noise levels will exceed ETSI and GR-63 requirements. Power filters

text: The PSS-8 shelf supports both AC and DC Power filter cards. 8DC30T 8DC30T card is a DC power filter card with full-featured CRU (F-CRU) capability on the PSS-8 shelf. This card type is applicable only for the F-CRU card on the PSS-8 shelf. The F-CRU timing module is integrated on the DC power supply unit of the PSS-8 shelf. 8DC30T2 The 8DC30T2 (a variant of 8DC30T card) is a DC power filter card with Full-featured CRU (F-CRU) capability on the PSS-8 shelf. PSS-8 shelf equipped with 8DC30T2 card does not support the BITS and output timing functionality. Apart from this all other functionality are similar to 8DC30T card. Note: BITS and output timing function does not support PSS-8 equipped with only 8DC30T2 or 8DC30T2 and 8DC30T/8DC30 cards.

The PF-DC card accepts DC input and provides power supply to other parts of the shelf. The power supplies are available with, or without, voltage monitoring ports. Power filters with input power monitoring are compatible with the power filters of the same size without input power monitoring. The PF-DC card supports the LOW VOLTAGE CUT-OFF (LVCO) function. The current rating of 8DC30 is 30.7A and the breaker at TRU is recommended to be 35A as maximum.

External interfaces The 16DC65 card has the following external interfaces on the faceplate: • Power connector • Card status LED • Power present LED (>35 V) and its label • EPS status LED: for active/standby indication of the timing function • Voltage measurement points and its label Appropriate cables are provided with ETSI and ANSI installation kits. The details are shown in the 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-16II) Release 23.6 Installation and System Turn-Up Guide. PF (16DC65) front view

section_path: 2 Shelves and common equipment/cards > 2.22 PSS-32 and PSS-16 Power filter cards (PFs) > 2.22.1 Introduction
text: Battery plant redundant feeds are brought into 1830 PSS-32 and 1830 PSS-16 shelves through two redundant power filter (PF) modules. External (typically, battery generated) DC voltages are filtered by the two PFs and distributed within the shelf by a copper power plane. Each PF provides the 3.6V service voltage that is distributed by the backplane. PFs also provide power to the USRPNL panel in the main shelf. The PF contains a circuit breaker on its faceplate that protects the battery feed. The PF module is also the source of a shared (Stratum 3 accuracy, +4.6 ppm) precision clock source that is used to generate the Wavelength Tracker modulation and serve as a high precision clock source for other transmission-related services.

The PF module is also the source of a shared (Stratum 3 accuracy, +4.6 ppm) precision clock source that is used to generate the Wavelength Tracker modulation and serve as a high precision clock source for other transmission-related services. Note: The PFDCA is the only power filter that does not include a circuit breaker or Wavelength Tracker capability. Point-to-point connections from each PF slot to all function slots, as well as the controller slots, carry this clock signal. Providing these clock sources on the PF eliminates the need to add highly stable 4.6-ppm oscillators on every circuit card that provides a Wavelength Tracker encode or decode function. The PF module also contains a temperature sensor that measures inlet air temperature which is then used to provide input into FAN control algorithm (adjusting FAN speed based on inlet temperature). The power supplies are available with, or without, voltage monitoring ports. Power filters with input power monitoring are compatible with the power filters of the same size without input power monitoring. Power filters are available with or without voltage monitoring that provide the following current capacities: • 1830 PSS-32 − 20A − 30A − 50A − 60A − 70A • 1830 PSS-16 − 20A − 35A
